title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, and Communications
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook captures Redwood Inference's standardized approach to on-call and incident response. It covers the incident lifecycle (detection, triage, mitigation, recovery, and retrospective), operational runbooks for common outage classes, postmortem and blameless review guidance, on-call rotations and responsibilities, scheduled game days, plus templates for status page updates and customer communications. The audience is SREs, platform engineers, product/infra owners, and support who will run or support incidents.

Goals and principles:
- Minimize customer impact while preserving safety and correctness.
- Prioritize fast, observable mitigation over speculative long-term fixes.
- Maintain blameless postmortems with actionable remediation.
- Keep status communications clear, frequent, and empathetic.

1) Incident lifecycle (high level)

1. Detection
- Sources: automated alerts, internal dashboards, external customer reports, support tickets, and partner monitoring.
- Primary detection channels: PagerDuty (high-severity), Slack #oncall (low/medium), status.redwood.ai (public updates).
- Typical indicators: API 5xx rate increase, latency P95 > 2x SLO, GPU pool unavailable, high KV cache miss rates.

2. Triage (first 15 minutes)
- On-call engineer acknowledges the alert within the PagerDuty timeout window (default 2 mins).
- Determine scope: customer-facing impact (yes/no), internal-only degradation, or scheduled maintenance.
- Assign incident severity (P1/P2/P3) per table below.

Severity definition table:
| Severity | Definition | PagerDuty urgency | Response window | Incident Lead | Customer comms |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Total outage or >25% of requests failing for major customers | High | 15 min | Primary on-call + Eng SRE | Immediate (status page + customer pings) |
| P2 | Significant degradation (latency or error spike) affecting multiple customers | High | 30 min | Primary on-call | Status page / customer advisory within 1 hour |
| P3 | Localized impact, non-production, or minor degradation | Normal | 4 hours | Service owner / secondary on-call | Internal incident note; optional customer update |

3. Mitigation and containment
- Short-term mitigation is the priority. Steps are in service-specific runbooks. If no runbook exists, follow the generic mitigation steps below.
- Maintain communication in the incident Slack channel: summary, hypothesis, mitigations tried, and next steps. Establish a dedicated private channel #incident-<id>.

Short-term mitigation checklist (generic):
1. Collect context: logs, traces, dashboard links (include timestamp UTC).
2. Confirm alert validity and rollback any suspicious config changes.
3. If traffic-related, failover or reduce injection: adjust routing, scale capacity, enable throttles.
4. If model-serving degradation, fallback to verified model variant or warm standby pool.
5. If safety/incorrect outputs, pause affected routes and notify product/security.
6. If mitigation succeeds, monitor for regression 30–60 minutes before marking recovered.

4. Recovery and verification
- Restore normal service gradually and validate against SLOs: error rate, latency P95, and success rate by route.
- Notify customers via status page and existing ticket threads when root cause is known and mitigations are in place.

5. Retrospective and postmortem
- Initiate a blameless postmortem for P1/P2 incidents. Postmortem must be published within 5 business days and include timeline, root cause, action items with owners and due dates, and verification plan.

2) Runbook structure and examples

Runbook template (every runbook should include these sections):
- Runbook name and owner (team)
- Symptoms & indicators (alert names, dashboard panels)
- Impact scope and severity mapping
- Immediate mitigation steps (numbered)
- Diagnostics commands and queries (CLI/log examples)
- Rollback/fallback actions and safety checks
- Escalation path and contacts
- Post-incident verification steps

Example runbook: API 5xx spike
- Owner: eng-platform / serving-runtime
- Symptoms: 5xx rate > 5% sustained for 5 minutes; alert: api-5xx-rate-high
- Immediate steps:
  1. Acknowledge PagerDuty, open #incident-<id>.
  2. Check release window and deploy logs: `gitops get-deploys --since 30m` and `kubectl get pods -l app=api -o wide`.
  3. Throttle non-essential background tasks: `k8s scale --replicas=0 job/bulk-embedding` (if applicable).
  4. If recent deploy suspected, trigger automated rollback: `gitops rollback <service> <previous-revision>`; otherwise scale up API workers in the affected region.
  5. Enable per-route circuit breaker or fall back to a lower-cost model variant.
  6. If GPU-serving related, check job queue, NVLink errors, and restart affected nodes via `fleetctl reboot <node>` with caution.
- Diagnostics snippets:
  - Example query (Prometheus): `sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (service)`
  - Example log search: `logger query "ERROR" service=api start="-30m"`

Example runbook: Dedicated GPU pool outage
- Owner: eng-infra / gpu-fleet
- Symptoms: `gpu-nodes-unavailable` alert; service-level degrade for Dedicated customers in region-us-west
- Steps:
  1. Contact cloud provider console & verify health events.
  2. Move critical workloads to standby pools: update autoscaler pools and reassign shards.
  3. Execute emergency scaling: `terraform apply -var='extra_gpu_count=8'` (use IaC runbook with change-control).
  4. If node-level failures, cordon and drain nodes: `kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets` and schedule hardware restart.
  5. Escalate to infra on-call and notify Sales for impacted dedicated customers.

3) Escalation & ownership matrix
- Primary on-call: owns initial triage and short-term mitigation.
- Secondary on-call: supports diagnostics and takes over if primary cannot.
- Eng SRE lead: coordinates cross-team responses for P1s.
- Product/feature owner: responsible for customer-impacting product decisions.
- Customer Success & Sales: owned by customer-success to coordinate handoffs and external comms for enterprise customers.

Escalation phone tree (primary contact methods): PagerDuty -> Slack -> Phone -> Executive on-call. All contacts maintained in internal directory.

4) On-call rotations and responsibilities
- Rotations are maintained in PagerDuty and synced to the on-call calendar. Standard rotation is 1 week for platform and SRE teams; 2 weeks for smaller feature teams by agreement.
- Shift handoff checklist (before midnight UTC):
  - Summarize active incidents, mitigations, and outstanding action items.
  - Export important logs and links to the handoff note in the rotation calendar.
  - Confirm pager and Slack notifications are functional.
- Responsibilities while on-call:
  - Acknowledge and own alerts within the configured window.
  - Keep the incident channel updated every 15 minutes for P1s and hourly for P2s.
  - Execute runbook steps, coordinate escalations, and produce an initial incident timeline.
  - After incident, schedule or document action items for the owning teams.

5) Game days and exercises
- Purpose: validate runbooks, test failovers, and reduce cognitive load under stress.
- Cadence: quarterly for platform-wide exercises and monthly for team-level scenarios.
- Typical game day scenarios:
  - Region-level GPU exhaustion (simulate node loss).
  - Model variant regression (simulate degraded outputs).
  - Large customer traffic spike (simulate synthetic load).
- Game day checklist:
  1. Pre-announce to teams & set safe-guards (timebox, customer-impact throttles).
  2. Run the scenario with a recorded timeline.
  3. Conduct a 90-minute post-exercise review and publish action items within 3 business days.

6) Postmortem guidance (blameless reviews)
- Timeline: create draft within 48 hours, publish final postmortem within 5 business days for P1/P2.
- Required sections:
  1. Summary (concise impact statement)
  2. Timeline (UTC timestamps, short actions)
  3. Root cause analysis (why the change/failure happened)
  4. Contributing factors (systemic issues)
  5. Corrective actions (owner + due date)
  6. Verification plan (how we will confirm remediation)
- Action items: prioritize at most 5 high-impact items; include owners and verification criteria. Adopt follow-up in the weekly reliability sync if not closed by due date.

7) Status page & customer communication templates

Status page template (short):
- Title: Incident — [Service] degraded in [region]
- Impact: Short description of impacted customers and functionality (who, what, when).
- Current status: investigating / identified / mitigated / resolved
- Next update: time in UTC and expected cadence (e.g., 30 min)
- Technical detail: short description of cause and mitigation (non-confidential)
- Owner: on-call lead name and team

Customer email template (enterprise customers)
Subject: Incident affecting [service] in [region] — current status
Hello [Customer name],

We detected an incident impacting [service] in [region] beginning at [UTC time]. Impact: [short summary]. Our on-call team has implemented a mitigation to [action]. We will continue to monitor and provide updates every [30 / 60] minutes.

If you have critical workflows impacted, please reply to this email or open a ticket and we will prioritize.

Best,
[On-call lead] — Redwood Inference Operations

Post-resolution customer summary (final):
- Summary of root cause (non-sensitive), sequence of events, and actions taken.
- Timeline of events (UTC).
- Any customer-facing changes they should make (e.g., TTL tuning, retry windows).
- Contact for follow-up and remediation validation.

8) Metrics, SLOs, and alert thresholds (examples)
- API availability SLO: 99.95% monthly (excludes scheduled maintenance). Alert when 30m rolling availability < 99.5%.
- Latency SLO (generation endpoint): P95 < 600ms. Alert when P95 > 1200ms for 5m.
- Error rate: 5xx < 0.1% for production traffic. Alert when 5xx > 1% sustained for 5m.

9) Tooling & observability links (maintain current links in the runbook)
- PagerDuty: https://redwood.pagerduty.com (internal)
- Status page: https://status.redwood.ai
- Dashboards: Grafana /dashboards/serving-runtime and /dashboards/api-performance
- Playbook repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/runbooks.git

10) Appendix: incident channel checklist (copy into every #incident-<id>)
- Title and incident ID
- Severity and impacted regions/customers
- Timestamps (UTC) and short timeline
- Primary/Secondary on-call with contact links
- Links: dashboards, logs, recent deploys, status page draft, related tickets

If you discover gaps in runbooks or tooling while executing this playbook, document them in the runbook repo and tag the reliability backlog. For questions or suggested edits, contact the Eng SRE documentation owner (Miguel Alvarez).

End of playbook.
